title: Stream timeout can block indefinitely while joining the pump
reasoning: After the command deadline expires, process_stream sets the stop event and performs an unbounded thread.join(). The pump only checks that event after the stream iterator yields. A silent process or blocked transport can therefore keep the pump blocked indefinitely, preventing the timeout result from reaching the caller.
reproduction: Consume process_stream with a short timeout, poll_fn returning None, and an iterator blocked waiting for an event. The consumer remains blocked past the deadline until the iterator is externally released.
recommendation: Provide a cancellation mechanism that interrupts the underlying stream read, and bound pump shutdown by an explicit cleanup deadline.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included stream processor test only checks decoding invalid UTF-8; it does not exercise timeouts or blocked iterators.
suggestedRegressionTest: Test silent and partially emitting blocked streams, asserting bounded timeout completion and pump termination. Release blocked test iterators in teardown.
minimumFixScope: Stream pump cancellation and process_stream shutdown.
